chunks: So wait with patience for the judgement of your Lord, and do not be like (onah) of the fish who called (to his Lord) when he was choked with anger.

key_terms.كَصَاحِبِ الْحُوتِ: like the companion of the fish
key_terms.لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ: for the judgement of your Lord

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'choked with anger' in the context of Surah Al-Qalam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Qalam is often linked to the broader narrative of Prophet Yunus (AS), serving as a divine instruction for the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to maintain steadfastness against the impatience of his detractors. The term 'makhum' (choked with anger) is interpreted by scholars like Allamah Tabatabai as a state of suppressed emotion where one calls out to God, highlighting the spiritual necessity of self-restraint and remembrance during trials.
